questions.question: A patient with recurrent symptomatic AF has a prior myocardial infarction, ventricular scar and LVEF 35%. Which proposed rhythm-maintenance strategy should be avoided because of this substrate?
options: Catheter-ablation evaluation after assessment of candidacy
Amiodarone after review of organ toxicity and interactions
Dofetilide with protocol-based monitored initiation where available
Flecainide for long-term sinus-rhythm maintenance
questions.explanation:
Structural Substrate and Class IC Drug Selection

Correct answer: Flecainide for long-term sinus-rhythm maintenance

Class IC and Infarct Scar

**Avoid flecainide with previous MI, ventricular scar or significant structural myocardial disease.**

Conduction slowing can promote dangerous ventricular reentry.

Choose by Substrate

**Amiodarone or dofetilide may be options in selected HFrEF patients.**

Eligibility depends on QT, kidney function, interactions and availability.

**Consider ablation and optimize the underlying disease.**

Restoring sinus rhythm pharmacologically is not beneficial if the chosen agent increases proarrhythmia.

Catheter-ablation evaluation after assessment of candidacy: Ablation can improve symptoms and selected outcomes in appropriate AF patients with HFrEF. Prior infarction does not itself rule out an electrophysiology assessment for this strategy.

Amiodarone after review of organ toxicity and interactions: Amiodarone is a guideline-supported option in selected HFrEF patients, although substantial extracardiac toxicity and interactions require careful assessment. It is not restricted in the same way as flecainide by the supplied infarct-scar substrate.

Dofetilide with protocol-based monitored initiation where available: Dofetilide can be used in selected HFrEF patients with renal, QT and interaction safeguards. Its initiation requirements are important, but it is not the class IC substrate-related exclusion tested here.

    • Conduction slowing can promote dangerous ventricular reentry.

Choose by Substrate

  • Amiodarone or dofetilide may be options in selected HFrEF patients.
    • Eligibility depends on QT, kidney function, interactions and availability.
  • Consider ablation and optimize the underlying disease.
    • Restoring sinus rhythm pharmacologically is not beneficial if the chosen agent increases proarrhythmia.

Other Options

  • Catheter-ablation evaluation after assessment of candidacy: Ablation can improve symptoms and selected outcomes in appropriate AF patients with HFrEF. Prior infarction does not itself rule out an electrophysiology assessment for this strategy.
  • Amiodarone after review of organ toxicity and interactions: Amiodarone is a guideline-supported option in selected HFrEF patients, although substantial extracardiac toxicity and interactions require careful assessment. It is not restricted in the same way as flecainide by the supplied infarct-scar substrate.
  • Dofetilide with protocol-based monitored initiation where available: Dofetilide can be used in selected HFrEF patients with renal, QT and interaction safeguards. Its initiation requirements are important, but it is not the class IC substrate-related exclusion tested here.

  • ACC/AHA/ACCP/HRS AF guideline, 2023
  • ESC atrial fibrillation guideline, 2024

questions.question: A patient with infrequent symptomatic paroxysmal AF has no prior MI, significant structural disease, pre-excitation or conduction disorder. A single-dose flecainide strategy has been effective and safe during monitored testing. Which instruction is an essential component of the outpatient plan?
options: Use the prescribed AV nodal blocker with the class IC dose to reduce the risk of one-to-one atrial flutter conduction
Omit AV nodal treatment because flecainide reliably prevents rapid flutter conduction
Repeat the full conversion dose hourly until palpitations stop
Stop anticoagulation whenever the pill restores sinus rhythm
questions.explanation:
Pill-in-the-Pocket Conversion With Class IC Therapy

Correct answer: Use the prescribed AV nodal blocker with the class IC dose to reduce the risk of one-to-one atrial flutter conduction

Pill-in-the-Pocket Flecainide

**Use the prescribed AV nodal blocker to reduce 1:1 flutter conduction risk.**

Class IC treatment can organize AF into an atrial flutter circuit.

Selection and Instructions

**Prior monitored testing and absence of significant structural/conduction disease are essential.**

A common single dose is 200 mg below 70 kg or 300 mg at ≥70 kg, according to the supervised plan.

**Provide clear escalation and repeat-dose limits.**

Do not apply this plan to pre-excited AF or unstable symptoms.

Omit AV nodal treatment because flecainide reliably prevents rapid flutter conduction: Class IC treatment can organize AF into flutter while slowing its atrial cycle enough to permit rapid AV conduction. It does not reliably protect the AV node against a one-to-one response.

Repeat the full conversion dose hourly until palpitations stop: The strategy is a prescribed single dose with a defined rescue plan, not unrestricted repeated loading. Repeated high doses can cause accumulation, QRS widening, bradycardia or ventricular proarrhythmia.

Stop anticoagulation whenever the pill restores sinus rhythm: Conversion does not by itself remove the patient’s embolic-risk indication or pericardioversion precautions. Stroke prevention is assessed independently from symptom termination.

questions.question: Dofetilide is selected for an eligible AF patient in a setting where it is available. Calculated creatinine clearance is 48 mL/min, baseline QTc is 420 ms with a narrow QRS, and potassium, magnesium and interaction review are satisfactory. Which initial approach matches US labelling?
options: 500 micrograms twice daily with the same monitoring
250 micrograms twice daily with protocol-based inpatient ECG monitoring
125 micrograms twice daily as the standard renal starting category
250 micrograms twice daily with the first ECG check at an outpatient visit
questions.explanation:
Dofetilide Initiation and Renal Dosing

Correct answer: 250 micrograms twice daily with protocol-based inpatient ECG monitoring

Dofetilide Renal Dosing

**CrCl 40–60 mL/min → 250 micrograms twice daily.**

Use Cockcroft–Gault and the QT-guided initiation protocol.

Monitored Initiation

**Hospital ECG monitoring for at least three days**, with adequate observation after conversion.

**Exclude prohibited interactions and correct potassium/magnesium.**

Lower CrCl requires lower dosing; CrCl <20 is contraindicated. Repeat QT and renal assessment with clinical change.

Rhythm-maintenance drug | Selection and principal safeguards

Dofetilide | Selected HFrEF use; CrCl-based dose, inpatient initiation, serial QT; contraindicated at CrCl <20 mL/min

Amiodarone | Selected HFrEF use; organ toxicity and interactions limit use; thyroid/liver and symptom-directed pulmonary surveillance

Dronedarone | 400 mg twice daily in eligible nonpermanent AF; avoid permanent AF, NYHA III–IV HF or decompensation within 4 weeks under US 2023 guidance

Sotalol | Beta blockade plus class III effect; renal dose selection, QT/electrolyte and bradycardia surveillance; generally avoid in HFrEF under US 2023 guidance

500 micrograms twice daily with the same monitoring: Five hundred micrograms twice daily is the initial renal category above 60 mL/min when other criteria permit. At 48 mL/min, that dose exceeds the labelled starting renal category.

125 micrograms twice daily as the standard renal starting category: This is the labelled starting category for clearance 20 to below 40 mL/min. A clinician may select a lower individualized dose, but it is not the standard category corresponding to the supplied clearance.

250 micrograms twice daily with the first ECG check at an outpatient visit: The renal dose is correct, but initiation or reinitiation requires continuous monitored inpatient care with serial QT assessment and resuscitation capability. A correct milligram or microgram amount does not replace the required initiation setting.

questions.question: A patient taking amiodarone for AF reports progressive dry cough and dyspnea after several months. Examination and initial assessment do not establish congestion or infection. Which next approach best addresses an important treatment-related possibility?
options: Use normal thyroid tests to exclude clinically important amiodarone toxicity
Attribute symptoms to AF recurrence without checking pulmonary disease
Evaluate for amiodarone pulmonary toxicity with chest imaging and clinical differential assessment
Continue unchanged treatment because a low maintenance dose excludes lung injury
questions.explanation:
Monitoring During Long-Term Amiodarone Treatment

Correct answer: Evaluate for amiodarone pulmonary toxicity with chest imaging and clinical differential assessment

Amiodarone Pulmonary Toxicity

**New cough and dyspnea require investigation**, including chest imaging and the competing diagnoses of HF and infection.

Drug Review

**Suspected toxicity may require withdrawal and specialist treatment.**

A normal earlier chest study does not exclude newly developed injury.

**Monitor thyroid, liver, ECG and relevant symptoms throughout therapy.**

The long half-life means adverse effects can persist after stopping; QT prolongation is not the only important toxicity.

Use normal thyroid tests to exclude clinically important amiodarone toxicity: Thyroid assessment detects one toxicity domain. Normal thyroid function does not exclude interstitial lung disease, hepatic injury or other amiodarone adverse effects.

Attribute symptoms to AF recurrence without checking pulmonary disease: AF can cause dyspnea, but a persistent dry cough and drug exposure require assessment of pulmonary causes. A rhythm explanation should be demonstrated rather than used to bypass a potentially serious adverse effect.

Continue unchanged treatment because a low maintenance dose excludes lung injury: Pulmonary toxicity can occur at lower maintenance doses and depends on cumulative exposure and susceptibility. Dose alone cannot safely exclude it in a symptomatic patient.

ACC/AHA/ACCP/HRS AF guideline, 2023 — https://doi.org/10.1161/CIR.0000000000001193

ESC atrial fibrillation guideline, 2024 — https://doi.org/10.1093/eurheartj/ehae176

questions.question: A patient with AF diagnosed three months ago and cardiovascular risk factors asks what EAST-AFNET 4 established. Which interpretation is most accurate?
options: An early rhythm-control strategy reduced a composite cardiovascular outcome compared with usual care in the studied population
The comparison established the benefit of first-line ablation over first-line antiarrhythmic medication
Restoration of sinus rhythm removed the need for anticoagulation
The comparison primarily established a strict rate-control target in recently diagnosed AF
questions.explanation:
Early Rhythm Control: EAST-AFNET 4

Correct answer: An early rhythm-control strategy reduced a composite cardiovascular outcome compared with usual care in the studied population

EAST-AFNET 4

**Early rhythm control reduced a composite cardiovascular outcome** in patients with recently diagnosed AF and cardiovascular conditions.

Strategy, Not One Drug

**Treatment included selected drugs and ablation.**

The result does not establish that every antiarrhythmic has equal benefit.

**Continue anticoagulation and comorbidity management as indicated.**

Apparent sinus rhythm does not remove baseline embolic risk or replace broader AF care.

The comparison established the benefit of first-line ablation over first-line antiarrhythmic medication: The intervention was an early rhythm-control strategy using drugs and ablation as appropriate, not a randomized comparison between these two methods. The result cannot be assigned exclusively to ablation.

Restoration of sinus rhythm removed the need for anticoagulation: Stroke prevention and cardiovascular care continued as indicated. The study does not establish rhythm success as permission to withdraw anticoagulation in a high-risk patient.

The comparison primarily established a strict rate-control target in recently diagnosed AF: The randomized strategy concerned early restoration and maintenance of sinus rhythm, not strict versus lenient ventricular rate targets. Rate control could be used within care, but it was not the tested intervention.

EAST-AFNET 4 randomized trial, 2020 — https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMoa2019422

questions.question: A patient asks what the original randomized ADVENT trial established about pulsed-field ablation for drug-refractory paroxysmal AF. Which answer is most accurate?
options: Pulsed-field ablation was noninferior to thermal ablation for the prespecified one-year efficacy and safety endpoints
Pulsed-field ablation was superior for efficacy and noninferior for serious procedural safety events
Pulsed-field ablation was noninferior for efficacy and superior for serious procedural safety events
Pulsed-field ablation was tested against medical rhythm control in persistent AF
questions.explanation:
Pulsed-Field Versus Thermal AF Ablation

Correct answer: Pulsed-field ablation was noninferior to thermal ablation for the prespecified one-year efficacy and safety endpoints

ADVENT

**Pulsed-field ablation was noninferior to thermal ablation** for the prespecified one-year efficacy and safety endpoints in drug-refractory paroxysmal AF.

What Noninferiority Means

**The trial did not prove superiority for every outcome or absence of rare harm.**

Device, operator and population matter.

**Separate acute procedural success from long-term rhythm control.**

Follow-up surveillance and ongoing stroke-prevention assessment remain necessary.

Pulsed-field ablation was superior for efficacy and noninferior for serious procedural safety events: ADVENT established noninferiority for the prespecified efficacy endpoint; a demonstrated superiority claim is a different statistical conclusion and was not the original trial result.

Pulsed-field ablation was noninferior for efficacy and superior for serious procedural safety events: Relative tissue selectivity is clinically relevant, but the original randomized safety conclusion was noninferiority rather than superiority. Other access, embolic and perforation risks remain possible.

Pulsed-field ablation was tested against medical rhythm control in persistent AF: ADVENT compared pulsed-field with thermal catheter ablation in drug-refractory paroxysmal AF. This option changes both the comparator and the enrolled AF pattern.

questions.question: A patient has sustained regular monomorphic VT at 158/min, BP 126/78 mmHg and normal mentation without congestion or ischemic discomfort. LVEF is 50%, renal function is normal, and baseline QT is not prolonged. With continuous ECG/BP monitoring and cardioversion available, which initial regimen follows the AHA 2025 stable wide-QRS tachycardia algorithm?
options: Amiodarone 150 mg over ten minutes with concurrent procainamide loading at 20–50 mg/min
Amiodarone 300 mg by rapid IV push, followed by assessment for a further 150 mg
Procainamide maintenance at 1–4 mg/min as the initial infusion, with loading deferred until recurrence
Procainamide 20–50 mg/min, stopping for suppression, hypotension, QRS widening greater than 50%, or 17 mg/kg
questions.explanation:
Drug Selection for Tolerated Monomorphic VT

Correct answer: Procainamide 20–50 mg/min, stopping for suppression, hypotension, QRS widening greater than 50%, or 17 mg/kg

Procainamide for Tolerated VT

**20–50 mg/min IV**, stopping at termination, hypotension, QRS widening >50% or total 17 mg/kg.

Maintenance 1–4 mg/min may follow in suitable patients.

Eligibility and Monitoring

**Avoid prolonged QT or significant HF**, and monitor ECG/BP continuously.

**Deterioration requires immediate electrical treatment.**

A stable initial BP does not guarantee continued tolerance; keep cardioversion ready.

Amiodarone 150 mg over ten minutes with concurrent procainamide loading at 20–50 mg/min: Either agent can be considered individually in suitable patients, but concurrent loading is not the algorithm strategy. Combined conduction and repolarization effects increase hypotension and proarrhythmia; reassess and obtain expert guidance rather than routinely stacking drugs.

Amiodarone 300 mg by rapid IV push, followed by assessment for a further 150 mg: This uses the shock-refractory VF/pulseless-VT arrest bolus sequence. For tolerated VT with a pulse, the algorithm instead gives amiodarone 150 mg over ten minutes, with subsequent infusion as appropriate.

Procainamide maintenance at 1–4 mg/min as the initial infusion, with loading deferred until recurrence: This is a maintenance rate after appropriate loading and reassessment. It is not the algorithm loading regimen for converting the ongoing sustained ventricular tachycardia.

questions.question: When discussing drug conversion of tolerated regular wide-complex tachycardia, which statement accurately describes PROCAMIO?
options: Procainamide produced fewer major acute cardiac adverse events and more terminations within 40 minutes than amiodarone in the studied population
Procainamide improved long-term survival compared with amiodarone after resuscitated VF
Amiodarone produced more terminations within 40 minutes, while procainamide caused fewer adverse events
Procainamide and amiodarone were compared with immediate cardioversion as a third randomized strategy
questions.explanation:
Interpreting the PROCAMIO Trial

Correct answer: Procainamide produced fewer major acute cardiac adverse events and more terminations within 40 minutes than amiodarone in the studied population

PROCAMIO

**Procainamide caused fewer major acute cardiac adverse events and more terminations by 40 minutes** than amiodarone in tolerated wide-complex tachycardia.

Population Limits

**Do not extrapolate to cardiac arrest or unstable VT.**

The small acute comparison does not establish long-term survival superiority.

**Choose the drug with QT, ventricular function and BP in mind.**

Trial benefit does not override an individual contraindication.

PROCAMIO outcome within 40 minutes | Procainamide | Amiodarone

Major cardiac adverse events | 9% | 41%

Tachycardia termination | 67% | 38%

Procainamide improved long-term survival compared with amiodarone after resuscitated VF: The trial assessed short-term treatment of tolerated monomorphic wide-complex tachycardia, not long-term survival after VF arrest. That population and endpoint require different evidence.

Amiodarone produced more terminations within 40 minutes, while procainamide caused fewer adverse events: The safety direction is consistent with the trial, but the termination result is reversed. Procainamide had the higher acute termination proportion as well as fewer major cardiac adverse events.

Procainamide and amiodarone were compared with immediate cardioversion as a third randomized strategy: The randomized comparison was between two drug regimens. Electrical cardioversion remained a rescue option but was not a third randomized treatment arm.

questions.question: During monitored procainamide treatment of tolerated monomorphic VT, QRS duration increases from 150 to 235 ms. BP remains adequate and the cumulative dose is only 9 mg/kg. Which action best follows the AHA infusion limits?
options: Continue to 17 mg/kg because blood pressure is preserved
Stop the infusion because QRS widening exceeds the specified safety limit
Reduce the infusion rate and continue until conversion because the dose is below the maximum
Add amiodarone while continuing procainamide to improve the termination rate
questions.explanation:
Procainamide Infusion Stopping Criteria

Correct answer: Stop the infusion because QRS widening exceeds the specified safety limit

QRS Safety Limit

**Increase = (235−150)/150 ×100 = 56.7%.**

This exceeds the >50% procainamide stopping criterion.

Respond to the First Limit

**Stop despite an adequate BP and a cumulative dose below 17 mg/kg.**

Dose ceiling, hypotension, QRS widening and termination are alternative stopping conditions.

**Reassess rhythm and perfusion and arrange alternative treatment.**

Continued exposure can intensify conduction slowing and proarrhythmia.

Continue to 17 mg/kg because blood pressure is preserved: Seventeen mg/kg is a maximum dose, not an obligation to complete loading. Excessive QRS widening is an independent stopping criterion even before hypotension develops.

Reduce the infusion rate and continue until conversion because the dose is below the maximum: Slowing infusion can be relevant to some tolerability problems, but the algorithm specifies stopping when QRS duration increases by more than fifty percent. Continuing exposure disregards that independent limit.

Add amiodarone while continuing procainamide to improve the termination rate: Combining drugs can add hypotension and repolarization-related proarrhythmia. Failure to convert before a procainamide safety endpoint is reached calls for reassessment and an alternative strategy, not routine simultaneous loading.

questions.question: A patient has tolerated monomorphic VT with a pulse. After expert assessment, IV amiodarone is selected. Which initial regimen matches the AHA 2025 tachyarrhythmia-with-pulse algorithm?
options: Start 1 mg/min without the initial loading infusion
300 mg IV as a rapid arrest-dose bolus
150 mg IV over two minutes as the standard perfusing-rhythm load
150 mg IV over 10 minutes with continuous monitoring
questions.explanation:
Amiodarone Dosing in Perfusing VT Versus Cardiac Arrest

Correct answer: 150 mg IV over 10 minutes with continuous monitoring

Amiodarone in VT With a Pulse

**150 mg IV over 10 minutes**, then the appropriate monitored infusion.

The usual initial infusion is 1 mg/min for six hours.

Do Not Mix Arrest Protocols

**Shock-refractory VF/pulseless VT uses a different bolus sequence.**

A rapid arrest dose is not the standard treatment for a perfusing patient.

**Monitor hypotension, bradycardia and QT.**

Unstable monomorphic VT requires synchronized cardioversion; drugs must not delay it.

Start 1 mg/min without the initial loading infusion: One mg/min is the subsequent first-six-hour infusion in the algorithm. It is not the specified initial loading regimen when acute pharmacological conversion is selected.

300 mg IV as a rapid arrest-dose bolus: A 300-mg IV/IO bolus is the initial amiodarone regimen for shock-refractory VF/pVT during cardiac arrest. It should not be transferred unchanged to a perfusing patient, where rapid administration can cause marked hypotension.

150 mg IV over two minutes as the standard perfusing-rhythm load: The supplied algorithm specifies a ten-minute initial infusion. Compressing that infusion into a rapid bolus changes the safety profile, especially when pressure and ventricular function are vulnerable.

questions.question: Which statement correctly describes the original VANISH trial in ischemic cardiomyopathy with an ICD and VT despite antiarrhythmic therapy?
options: Ablation reduced a composite of death, VT storm or appropriate ICD shock compared with escalation of antiarrhythmic therapy
Ablation was compared with ICD implantation in patients without a device
Ablation was compared with no antiarrhythmic treatment in previously untreated VT
Ablation established a significant isolated survival advantage as its primary endpoint
questions.explanation:
The Original VANISH Trial: Comparator and Outcome

Correct answer: Ablation reduced a composite of death, VT storm or appropriate ICD shock compared with escalation of antiarrhythmic therapy

Original VANISH

**Ablation reduced death, VT storm or appropriate ICD shock as a composite** versus antiarrhythmic escalation in ischemic cardiomyopathy with VT despite drug therapy.

Comparator Matters

**The comparison was not ablation versus no treatment.**

Escalation included protocol-based amiodarone or mexiletine approaches.

**Composite benefit does not prove separate mortality reduction.**

Continue ICD and substrate-directed care; ablation does not erase all future arrhythmia risk.

Ablation was compared with ICD implantation in patients without a device: Participants already had an ICD. The trial addressed recurrent VT treatment on that background, not replacement of device implantation with ablation.

Ablation was compared with no antiarrhythmic treatment in previously untreated VT: The defining problem was VT despite antiarrhythmic therapy. The control strategy escalated medication rather than withholding treatment or studying a drug-naive first episode.

Ablation established a significant isolated survival advantage as its primary endpoint: The primary endpoint combined death, VT storm and appropriate shock. A significant composite result does not establish a significant mortality reduction considered alone.

VANISH randomized trial, 2016 — https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMoa1513614

ESC ventricular arrhythmias and sudden cardiac death guideline, 2022 — https://doi.org/10.1093/eurheartj/ehac262

questions.question: A patient with prior MI and an ICD develops clinically significant VT and is discussing initial ablation versus an antiarrhythmic strategy. Which interpretation best describes VANISH2?
options: Initial ablation reduced the prespecified composite outcome compared with a protocol-selected sotalol or amiodarone strategy in the studied ischemic population
The trial required failure of chronic amiodarone before randomization
The trial established ablation as a substitute for ICD protection
The trial compared initial ablation with mexiletine added to high-dose amiodarone in every control patient
questions.explanation:
Initial VT Ablation: Interpreting VANISH2

Correct answer: Initial ablation reduced the prespecified composite outcome compared with a protocol-selected sotalol or amiodarone strategy in the studied ischemic population

VANISH2

**Initial ablation reduced the prespecified composite versus protocol-selected sotalol or amiodarone** in ischemic cardiomyopathy with clinically significant VT.

Translation

**This tests an earlier strategy than original VANISH.**

Do not require drug failure simply because that was the original trial’s entry context.

**Match ischemic substrate and procedural expertise.**

Benefit and complications must be discussed; the trial does not establish universal superiority in nonischemic disease.

The trial required failure of chronic amiodarone before randomization: That description resembles the prior-drug-failure question addressed by the original VANISH trial. VANISH2 evaluated an initial ablation strategy rather than requiring chronic amiodarone failure.

The trial established ablation as a substitute for ICD protection: Participants had ICD protection, and device-related outcomes formed part of the assessment. The comparison did not test removing or withholding the ICD after successful ablation.

The trial compared initial ablation with mexiletine added to high-dose amiodarone in every control patient: The drug strategy used sotalol or amiodarone according to prespecified eligibility. A uniform mexiletine add-on comparator misidentifies the treatment tested.

questions.question: A patient with prior MI, ventricular scar and LVEF 36% has mildly symptomatic PVCs. Flecainide markedly reduces the Holter PVC count during a proposed treatment trial. Which interpretation should guide continued prescribing?
options: Continue flecainide if a beta blocker is added to prevent proarrhythmia
Continue flecainide because documented suppression establishes reduced sudden-death risk
Do not infer clinical benefit from PVC suppression; class IC treatment is unsafe in this infarct-scar setting
Substitute propafenone because the concern applies specifically to the two CAST drugs
questions.explanation:
Ventricular Ectopy Suppression After Myocardial Infarction

Correct answer: Do not infer clinical benefit from PVC suppression; class IC treatment is unsafe in this infarct-scar setting

CAST and Surrogate Endpoints

**Suppressing PVCs with class IC treatment after MI did not establish benefit and increased mortality risk.**

Infarct scar provides a substrate for proarrhythmia.

Prescribing Implication

**Do not continue flecainide because the Holter looks better.**

Evaluate symptoms, LV function, ischemia and appropriate alternatives.

**Distinguish normal-heart idiopathic ectopy from infarct-related disease.**

The same reduction in ectopy can have very different clinical consequences.

Continue flecainide if a beta blocker is added to prevent proarrhythmia: AV nodal protection can reduce rapid flutter conduction in selected AF patients receiving class IC drugs. It does not neutralize the ventricular proarrhythmic risk of flecainide in infarct scar.

Continue flecainide because documented suppression establishes reduced sudden-death risk: Suppression is a surrogate electrophysiological effect. CAST demonstrated excess mortality despite successful ectopy suppression in the relevant post-MI population.

Substitute propafenone because the concern applies specifically to the two CAST drugs: Drug-specific trial evidence informs a broader class IC restriction in prior MI or significant scar. Switching to another potent class IC sodium-channel blocker does not establish safety in this substrate.

CAST encainide/flecainide mortality report, 1991 — https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJM199103213241201

questions.question: A young adult with confirmed LQT1, prolonged QT and prior exertional syncope has no bronchospasm, significant bradycardia or AV block. Which preventive drug strategy best matches ESC guidance?
options: Use mexiletine as the routine first medication for LQT1
Use metoprolol as an equivalent preferred choice irrespective of genotype and prior symptoms
Use an appropriately titrated preferred nonselective beta blocker such as nadolol or propranolol
Use sotalol to combine beta blockade with an additional class III effect
questions.explanation:
Preventive Drug Treatment in Congenital Long-QT Syndrome

Correct answer: Use an appropriately titrated preferred nonselective beta blocker such as nadolol or propranolol

Beta Blockade in Congenital LQTS

**Nadolol or propranolol is preferred when tolerated.**

Adrenergic triggers are especially relevant in LQT1.

Comprehensive Prevention

**Titrate and assess adherence**, HR, BP and breakthrough events.

**Avoid QT-prolonging drugs and correct electrolytes.**

Persistent events require specialist assessment for additional therapy, denervation or ICD according to risk; a beta blocker is not the entire management plan.

Use mexiletine as the routine first medication for LQT1: Mexiletine targets late sodium current and has an established genotype-directed role in LQT3 with prolonged QT. It does not replace the preferred beta-blocker approach for this supplied LQT1 presentation.

Use metoprolol as an equivalent preferred choice irrespective of genotype and prior symptoms: Metoprolol can have clinical uses, but comparative evidence and ESC guidance favor nadolol or propranolol for LQTS prevention. Beta blockers should not be assumed interchangeable for this inherited syndrome.

Use sotalol to combine beta blockade with an additional class III effect: Sotalol prolongs repolarization and can provoke torsades. Its beta-blocking property does not make it an appropriate preventive substitute in congenital long-QT disease.

ESC ventricular arrhythmias and sudden cardiac death guideline, 2022 — https://doi.org/10.1093/eurheartj/ehac262

  • Use mexiletine as the routine first medication for LQT1: Mexiletine targets late sodium current and has an established genotype-directed role in LQT3 with prolonged QT. It does not replace the preferred beta-blocker approach for this supplied LQT1 presentation.
  • Use metoprolol as an equivalent preferred choice irrespective of genotype and prior symptoms: Metoprolol can have clinical uses, but comparative evidence and ESC guidance favor nadolol or propranolol for LQTS prevention. Beta blockers should not be assumed interchangeable for this inherited syndrome.
  • Use sotalol to combine beta blockade with an additional class III effect: Sotalol prolongs repolarization and can provoke torsades. Its beta-blocking property does not make it an appropriate preventive substitute in congenital long-QT disease.

questions.question: Which interpretation of DINAMIT and IRIS best explains why high early post-MI sudden-death risk does not by itself justify routine immediate prophylactic ICD implantation?
options: The results exclude an ICD indication for any later post-MI survivor
The devices failed to terminate ventricular arrhythmias in the early post-MI period
The trials established improved overall survival but poor cost-effectiveness
Early ICD implantation reduced arrhythmic or sudden deaths but did not improve overall survival in the studied populations
questions.explanation:
Early Post-MI ICD Trials and Competing Mortality

Correct answer: Early ICD implantation reduced arrhythmic or sudden deaths but did not improve overall survival in the studied populations

DINAMIT and IRIS

**Early prophylactic ICDs reduced arrhythmic/sudden deaths without improving overall survival.**

Competing nonarrhythmic mortality matters soon after MI.

Timing

**Optimize therapy and reassess EF after the guideline waiting period.**

Early low EF can improve with recovery and revascularization.

**Secondary prevention and reversible causes are separate assessments.**

These primary-prevention trials do not settle every sustained-VT presentation.

The results exclude an ICD indication for any later post-MI survivor: The timing and selection differ from chronic primary-prevention trials and secondary-prevention indications. An early negative trial does not invalidate later implantation when established criteria are met.

The devices failed to terminate ventricular arrhythmias in the early post-MI period: Lack of an overall survival advantage does not mean the devices had no antiarrhythmic efficacy. Cause-specific deaths and total mortality must be distinguished.

The trials established improved overall survival but poor cost-effectiveness: The limitation was not simply economic. The randomized early-implant strategies did not demonstrate the overall survival benefit required to support routine prophylactic use in those populations.

questions.question: Which statement accurately summarizes the original DANISH trial of prophylactic ICD therapy in nonischemic systolic HF?
options: ICD treatment significantly reduced all-cause mortality without reducing sudden death
ICD treatment reduced sudden cardiac death but did not significantly reduce all-cause mortality in the overall trial population
ICD treatment and control were proven equivalent for survival
The study compared CRT-defibrillators with medical treatment that excluded CRT
questions.explanation:
Interpreting DANISH Without Overstating a Negative Endpoint

Correct answer: ICD treatment reduced sudden cardiac death but did not significantly reduce all-cause mortality in the overall trial population

DANISH

**ICD therapy reduced sudden death but not overall all-cause mortality significantly** in the original nonischemic systolic-HF trial.

Individual Risk

**Age, comorbidity, competing death and background CRT influence net benefit.**

A neutral overall endpoint does not prove that no selected patient benefits.

**Use guideline-based shared decisions.**

Do not replace overall trial evidence with an unqualified subgroup or a single EF threshold.

ICD treatment significantly reduced all-cause mortality without reducing sudden death: This reverses the trial’s findings. Sudden death was reduced, while the overall all-cause mortality primary endpoint was not significantly lower.

ICD treatment and control were proven equivalent for survival: Failure to demonstrate superiority is not an equivalence result. The confidence interval includes different plausible effects and must be interpreted with trial design and population.

The study compared CRT-defibrillators with medical treatment that excluded CRT: CRT was used in a substantial proportion of both groups when indicated. The comparison tested added defibrillator protection on contemporary background care rather than CRT versus its absence.

DANISH randomized trial, 2016 — https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMoa1608029

AHA/ACC/HFSA heart failure guideline, 2022 — https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jacc.2021.12.012

questions.question: A patient with LVEF 30% soon after MI asks whether VEST proved that every patient awaiting primary-prevention reassessment should receive a wearable defibrillator. Which response is most accurate?
options: A secondary all-cause mortality finding establishes the primary arrhythmic endpoint as positive
VEST established a significant primary-endpoint benefit requiring universal post-MI use
VEST proved that a wearable device cannot terminate ventricular arrhythmia
VEST did not significantly reduce its primary arrhythmic-death endpoint in intention-to-treat analysis; temporary use requires individual assessment
questions.explanation:
Wearable Defibrillator Evidence After MI

Correct answer: VEST did not significantly reduce its primary arrhythmic-death endpoint in intention-to-treat analysis; temporary use requires individual assessment

VEST

**The primary arrhythmic-death endpoint was not significantly reduced in intention-to-treat analysis.**

Adherence and exposure are relevant but do not replace the randomized primary result.

Temporary Protection

**Consider a wearable device selectively during reassessment.**

Discuss wear time, limitations and the underlying recovery plan.

**Do not claim universal benefit or equivalence to an implanted ICD.**

Repeat EF and optimize therapy before the definitive prevention decision.

A secondary all-cause mortality finding establishes the primary arrhythmic endpoint as positive: Primary and secondary endpoints must remain distinct. An uncorrected secondary signal cannot be substituted for the prespecified primary result.

VEST established a significant primary-endpoint benefit requiring universal post-MI use: The primary arrhythmic-death comparison was not statistically significant. Selected temporary use should not be represented as a universal mandate derived from that trial.

VEST proved that a wearable device cannot terminate ventricular arrhythmia: A negative primary outcome does not mean the device cannot deliver an effective shock. Clinical effectiveness also depends on wear time, patient selection and competing causes of death.

questions.question: A patient taking dronedarone for recurrent AF now has sustained AF, and patient and team decide that no further restoration of sinus rhythm will be attempted. EF is 55%. What is the best medication decision?
options: Increase dronedarone to improve ventricular rate control
Continue dronedarone because preserved EF removes the major restriction
Discontinue dronedarone and use an appropriate rate-control strategy
Reduce dronedarone to once daily while accepting AF
questions.explanation:
Dronedarone in Permanent AF

Correct answer: Discontinue dronedarone and use an appropriate rate-control strategy

Rhythm Strategy Determines Eligibility

**Permanent AF means that restoration is no longer pursued.**

Dronedarone is used in suitable patients in sinus rhythm with a history of paroxysmal or persistent AF; it is not continued for accepted permanent AF.

Safety and Follow-up

**Also avoid recent decompensated symptomatic HF or NYHA IV HF under US labeling.**

The standard eligible-patient regimen is ==400 mg== twice daily with meals; review QT, liver function and interactions.

**Stroke prevention remains risk-based**, independent of stopping the antiarrhythmic.

Increase dronedarone to improve ventricular rate control: Dose escalation does not make permanent-AF treatment appropriate; the drug is not a substitute for a suitable rate-control plan.

Continue dronedarone because preserved EF removes the major restriction: Permanent AF is itself a contraindication; preserved EF does not remove the excess adverse cardiovascular risk in this setting.

Reduce dronedarone to once daily while accepting AF: A lower off-label schedule does not establish safety in permanent AF and is not the recommended response to this change in rhythm strategy.

Dronedarone US prescribing information — https://products.sanofi.us/Multaq/multaq.pdf

options: Losartan

questions.explanation:
Dofetilide–Hydrochlorothiazide Interaction

Correct answer: Hydrochlorothiazide

Interaction Screening

**Hydrochlorothiazide is contraindicated, including combination tablets.**

The interaction is more than a generic warning about diuretic-associated potassium loss.

Safe Initiation

**Review all drugs before monitored initiation.**

Other prohibited combinations include verapamil, trimethoprim and cimetidine; use the current label for the complete list.

**Dose by CrCl and QT response**, with inpatient ECG monitoring for at least three days.

Correct potassium/magnesium and reassess after renal changes; an initially acceptable QT does not remove interaction risk.

Losartan: Losartan does not share the specified hydrochlorothiazide interaction; kidney function and potassium remain relevant to overall antiarrhythmic safety.

Amlodipine: This dihydropyridine is not the labeled dofetilide interaction in the question; blood-pressure effects still require routine clinical assessment.

Lisinopril: ACE inhibition is not the specific contraindicated interaction; renal deterioration or electrolyte changes still warrant review in a dofetilide-treated patient.

questions.question: A patient taking sotalol develops acute kidney injury. Heart rate is 52/min, narrow-QRS QTc is 525 ms, and potassium is normal. Which action is most appropriate?
options: Continue the same regimen because potassium is normal
Withhold further dosing and urgently reassess QT, renal dosing and rhythm
Increase the dose to prevent breakthrough ventricular arrhythmia
Add a second beta blocker while retaining the sotalol dose
questions.explanation:
Sotalol Accumulation and QT Prolongation

Correct answer: Withhold further dosing and urgently reassess QT, renal dosing and rhythm

Mechanism of Risk

**Sotalol combines beta blockade with delayed repolarization.**

Renal elimination requires an appropriate dosing interval; bradycardia and interacting QT-prolonging drugs increase risk.

Monitoring and Adjustment

**QT ==≥500 ms== requires dose reduction, interval extension or discontinuation under labeling.**

In this acute deterioration, withhold and obtain monitored specialist reassessment rather than an automatic outpatient adjustment.

**Recheck magnesium, potassium, creatinine and ECG.**

Reinitiation requires the appropriate monitored protocol; manage sustained ventricular arrhythmia immediately.

Continue the same regimen because potassium is normal: Normal potassium does not prevent concentration-dependent torsades; renal accumulation and bradycardia materially increase risk.

Increase the dose to prevent breakthrough ventricular arrhythmia: Additional exposure can intensify repolarization delay; prolonged QT is a toxicity warning, not an indication for escalation.

Add a second beta blocker while retaining the sotalol dose: Further slowing may worsen pause-related proarrhythmia and does not correct excessive sotalol exposure during kidney injury.

questions.question: An ACS patient has continuing ischemic discomfort, blood pressure 138/82 mm Hg and oxygen saturation 97% on room air. Tadalafil was taken eighteen hours earlier. Which immediate supportive-treatment plan is appropriate while definitive ACS care proceeds?
options: Give sublingual nitroglycerin because the current blood pressure is normal
Withhold nitrates and reassess pain and perfusion while expediting indicated coronary treatment
Use intravenous nitroglycerin because titration avoids the oral drug interaction
Give high-flow oxygen as the principal anti-ischemic treatment at the stated saturation
questions.explanation:
Recent Tadalafil Exposure During ACS

Correct answer: Withhold nitrates and reassess pain and perfusion while expediting indicated coronary treatment

Tadalafil–Nitrate Interaction

**Withhold nitrates for at least 48 hours after tadalafil.**

Shared amplification of cGMP-mediated vasodilation can cause profound hypotension.

Continue ACS Care

**Normal BP does not remove the interaction.**

Use appropriate alternatives while expediting reperfusion and antithrombotic care.

**Oxygen is not routinely needed at saturation 97%.**

Persistent pain requires reassessment; symptom treatment must not delay definitive coronary management.

Give sublingual nitroglycerin because the current blood pressure is normal: Normal baseline pressure does not remove the nitrate–PDE5 inhibitor interaction; tadalafil exposure within forty-eight hours makes nitrate-associated hypotension a serious concern.

Use intravenous nitroglycerin because titration avoids the oral drug interaction: The interaction is pharmacodynamic and persists with intravenous nitrate delivery; changing the route does not remove excessive cyclic-GMP-mediated vasodilation.

Give high-flow oxygen as the principal anti-ischemic treatment at the stated saturation: Supplemental oxygen treats hypoxemia, but routine use at this normal saturation has no established benefit and does not substitute for addressing continuing coronary ischemia.

questions.question: After anterior MI, a patient has heart rate 112/min, blood pressure 92/64 mm Hg, cool extremities and pulmonary congestion. No beta blocker has been administered. Which approach is appropriate?
options: Give intravenous metoprolol promptly to correct the tachycardia
Defer beta-blocker initiation, treat the unstable state, and reassess after stabilization
Start low-dose oral metoprolol now with close blood-pressure monitoring
Start carvedilol now to obtain its longer-term ventricular-remodeling benefit
questions.explanation:
Defer Early Beta Blockade During Low Output

Correct answer: Defer beta-blocker initiation, treat the unstable state, and reassess after stabilization

Beta Blockade During Hypoperfusion

**Cool extremities, low BP and congestion suggest an unstable low-output state.**

Tachycardia may be compensatory; acute negative inotropy can worsen shock.

Sequence Treatment

**Stabilize perfusion and treat the cause first.**

Reassess beta-blocker initiation after clinical compensation rather than applying routine early dosing despite instability.

**A later indication remains possible.**

questions.question: A clinician reviews contemporary randomized evidence for routine long-term beta blockers after an uncomplicated MI in patients with LVEF at least 50% and no other beta-blocker indication. Which interpretation is best supported by the 2025 individual-patient meta-analysis?
options: The findings support avoiding beta blockers during the acute admission as well as follow-up
Routine treatment established a mortality benefit equivalent to that in reduced-EF heart failure
Routine treatment did not reduce the composite of death, MI or heart failure in the preserved-EF population studied
The findings establish noninferiority of withdrawal in patients already receiving long-term treatment
questions.explanation:
Long-Term Beta Blockers With Preserved EF

Correct answer: Routine treatment did not reduce the composite of death, MI or heart failure in the preserved-EF population studied

Preserved-EF Post-MI Evidence

**The 2025 individual-patient meta-analysis found no reduction in death, MI or HF** with routine beta blockers in LVEF ≥50% without another indication.

Do Not Overextend

**This does not negate treatment for HFrEF, angina or arrhythmia.**

The mildly reduced-EF population is also distinct.

**Starting routine treatment and withdrawing established treatment are different questions.**

ABYSS does not justify a blanket instruction to abruptly stop every post-MI beta blocker.

The findings support avoiding beta blockers during the acute admission as well as follow-up: The analysis concerns long-term treatment in a selected EF population, not an instruction to abandon acute use when indicated or treatment for another condition.

Routine treatment established a mortality benefit equivalent to that in reduced-EF heart failure: Benefit in reduced-EF HF cannot be transferred to normal-EF post-MI patients; the contemporary pooled preserved-EF evidence did not demonstrate that claimed benefit.

The findings establish noninferiority of withdrawal in patients already receiving long-term treatment: Initiation-versus-no-treatment evidence does not establish universal withdrawal safety; ABYSS addressed interruption separately and did not demonstrate noninferiority of interruption.

questions.question: A patient with chronic angina is taking diltiazem. Ranolazine extended release is being considered after review of renal function, ECG and other drugs. Under the US prescribing information, what is the maximum ranolazine dose while diltiazem continues?
options: 500 mg twice daily
1000 mg twice daily
750 mg twice daily
375 mg twice daily
questions.explanation:
Ranolazine With Concurrent Diltiazem

Correct answer: 500 mg twice daily

Ranolazine With Diltiazem

**Limit ranolazine to 500 mg twice daily** with a moderate CYP3A inhibitor such as diltiazem under US labeling.

Mechanism and Safety

**Late sodium-current inhibition reduces ischemic calcium loading** with little direct HR/BP reduction.

**Review QT, liver disease, kidney function and interactions.**

Strong CYP3A inhibitors are a different, contraindicated combination; antianginal benefit is not proven mortality reduction.

1000 mg twice daily: This is the usual maximum without a relevant interacting inhibitor, but diltiazem increases ranolazine exposure and lowers the permitted maximum.

750 mg twice daily: Seven hundred fifty milligrams twice daily is a usual maximum in some European product information, but the question specifies the US prescribing information and its diltiazem interaction ceiling.

375 mg twice daily: Three hundred seventy-five milligrams twice daily is a starting dose in some European formulations; it is not the specified US maximum during moderate CYP3A inhibition.

questions.question: A patient with ACS has hemoglobin 8.4 g/dL without active bleeding. The team is reviewing the 2025 ACC/AHA recommendation and MINT evidence. Which interpretation is most appropriate?
options: The nonsignificant MINT result establishes equivalent safety of restrictive and liberal strategies
A seven-gram threshold remains the preferred ACS default because restrictive trials in other inpatients apply directly
MINT proved a statistically significant reduction in its primary endpoint with liberal transfusion
A liberal transfusion strategy toward hemoglobin around ten may be reasonable, with individualized benefit–risk assessment
questions.explanation:
Transfusion Strategy in ACS With Anemia

Correct answer: A liberal transfusion strategy toward hemoglobin around ten may be reasonable, with individualized benefit–risk assessment

Transfusion in ACS

**A liberal strategy toward hemoglobin around 10 g/dL may be reasonable** in selected ACS patients under the 2025 guidance.

Assess ischemia, volume tolerance and bleeding rather than applying one universal trigger.

MINT Interpretation

**MINT did not establish conventional statistical superiority for its primary endpoint.**

Its results did not exclude clinically important harm from the restrictive strategy.

**“May be reasonable” is not mandatory transfusion at every value below 10.**

Reassess response and avoid unnecessary volume exposure.

The nonsignificant MINT result establishes equivalent safety of restrictive and liberal strategies: A superiority comparison with P=0.07 does not establish equivalence; its confidence interval still permits clinically important harm from the restrictive strategy.

A seven-gram threshold remains the preferred ACS default because restrictive trials in other inpatients apply directly: Restrictive thresholds are supported in several other settings, but ACS-specific evidence and the named recommendation warrant separate interpretation rather than direct extrapolation.

MINT proved a statistically significant reduction in its primary endpoint with liberal transfusion: The primary comparison favored liberal treatment numerically but did not reach conventional statistical significance; overstating certainty misrepresents the trial.

MINT randomized transfusion trial, 2023 — https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMoa2307983

ACC/AHA/ACEP/NAEMSP/SCAI ACS guideline, 2025 — https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jacc.2024.11.009

questions.question: A stable patient has a seventy-percent unprotected left-main stenosis. A colleague cites ISCHEMIA as proof that an initial conservative strategy is equivalent for this anatomy. Which response is most appropriate?
options: Significant unprotected left-main disease was excluded, so the trial cannot justify that extrapolation
The overall neutral comparison supports medical therapy first for this left-main lesion
The conservative arm prohibited later angiography, limiting comparison with current practice
The lack of statistical significance establishes equivalence between strategies in stable CAD
questions.explanation:
Applying ISCHEMIA Beyond Its Enrollment Population

Correct answer: Significant unprotected left-main disease was excluded, so the trial cannot justify that extrapolation

ISCHEMIA Applicability

**Significant unprotected left-main disease was excluded.**

A 70% lesion therefore lies outside the population supporting the routine initial-strategy comparison.

Clinical Decision

**Assess prognostic anatomy and revascularization suitability.**

Do not use a broad “stable CAD” label to erase trial exclusions.

**Continue optimal medical treatment in either strategy.**

The trial compared initial management approaches, not effective medical care against no treatment.

The overall neutral comparison supports medical therapy first for this left-main lesion: An overall result applies within the population and strategies studied; it cannot establish a conservative-first conclusion for significant left-main disease that the trial excluded.

The conservative arm prohibited later angiography, limiting comparison with current practice: The conservative strategy allowed angiography and revascularization for clinical indications; the relevant limitation here is excluded anatomy rather than a permanent ban on invasive care.

The lack of statistical significance establishes equivalence between strategies in stable CAD: Failure to demonstrate superiority does not establish formal equivalence, and neither interpretation can extend the randomized comparison to this excluded anatomical subgroup.

questions.question: Which statement correctly distinguishes the original FAME and COURAGE randomized trials?
options: FAME compared FFR-selected PCI with medical therapy; COURAGE compared PCI with CABG
FAME compared PCI with medical therapy alone; COURAGE compared physiological with angiographic PCI guidance
FAME compared physiological versus angiographic PCI guidance; COURAGE compared initial PCI plus medical therapy with medical therapy alone
FAME compared FFR-guided with angiographic PCI; COURAGE compared intensive with moderate lipid lowering
questions.explanation:
FAME and COURAGE Answer Different Questions

Correct answer: FAME compared physiological versus angiographic PCI guidance; COURAGE compared initial PCI plus medical therapy with medical therapy alone

Different Randomized Questions

**FAME:** FFR-guided versus angiography-guided PCI.

It asks how to select lesions for intervention.

**COURAGE:** initial PCI plus optimal medical therapy versus medical therapy alone.

It asks whether adding PCI improves outcomes in the studied stable population.

Interpretation

**A guidance trial cannot establish benefit of PCI over no PCI.**

Similarly, a strategy trial does not settle every lesion-level physiological decision.

**Check population, comparator and endpoint** before translating either result to an individual patient.

FAME compared FFR-selected PCI with medical therapy; COURAGE compared PCI with CABG: The first comparison resembles FAME 2 rather than original FAME; COURAGE compared adding PCI to medical therapy and did not randomize patients between PCI and CABG.

FAME compared PCI with medical therapy alone; COURAGE compared physiological with angiographic PCI guidance: These trial designs are reversed: original FAME studied how to select lesions during planned multivessel PCI, whereas COURAGE studied adding initial PCI to medical therapy.

FAME compared FFR-guided with angiographic PCI; COURAGE compared intensive with moderate lipid lowering: The FAME description is correct, but COURAGE randomized the initial PCI strategy on a background of optimal medical therapy, not statin intensity as its assigned intervention.

COURAGE randomized trial, 2007 — https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMoa070829

questions.question: A patient uses a nitroglycerin patch continuously for chronic effort angina and reports declining benefit without a new unstable symptom pattern. Which schedule best addresses pharmacological tolerance?
options: Replace the patch every 12 hours without any gap
A daily patch-on period of 12–14 hours followed by 10–12 hours off
Increase patch strength while maintaining continuous exposure
Use the same patch for 48 hours before replacement
questions.explanation:
Preventing Nitrate Tolerance

Correct answer: A daily patch-on period of 12–14 hours followed by 10–12 hours off

Intermittent Exposure

**A nitrate-free interval restores responsiveness.**

Schedule coverage during usual exertional symptoms and plan the off-period individually.

Practical Care

**A patch is prophylaxis, not acute rescue therapy.**

Ensure an appropriate short-acting rescue plan and reassess worsening or new rest symptoms urgently.

**Monitor off-period symptoms and blood pressure.**

Other antianginal therapy may be needed; continuous exposure is not made effective merely by applying a fresh patch.

Replace the patch every 12 hours without any gap: Changing patches while maintaining continuous delivery does not provide the nitrate-free interval needed to limit tolerance.

Increase patch strength while maintaining continuous exposure: Dose escalation alone often fails to overcome tolerance and increases headache or hypotension without restoring reliable benefit.

Use the same patch for 48 hours before replacement: Extending wear does not create a controlled effective dosing schedule and does not address continuous-exposure tolerance appropriately.

questions.question: A patient taking nicorandil develops a persistent painful perianal ulcer. Evaluation excludes malignancy and infection, and drug causation is considered likely. Which medication strategy is most appropriate?
options: Continue nicorandil and add acid suppression
Stop nicorandil and arrange alternative antianginal treatment
Continue nicorandil and treat with topical corticosteroids alone
Halve nicorandil and continue until the ulcer closes
questions.explanation:
Nicorandil-Associated Ulceration

Correct answer: Stop nicorandil and arrange alternative antianginal treatment

Recognize the Adverse Effect

**Ulceration can involve oral, GI, perianal or cutaneous sites.**

It may occur after prolonged treatment and can cause fistula, perforation or bleeding.

Management

**Withdrawal is central when the association is suspected.**

Assess the lesion and complications; review analgesics and other drugs that increase injury or bleeding risk.

**Replace antianginal coverage according to heart rate, BP and ventricular function.**

Nicorandil’s potassium-channel and nitrate-like actions do not justify persisting with a serious adverse effect.

Continue nicorandil and add acid suppression: Acid suppression may treat acid-related upper GI disease but does not remove nicorandil-associated mucosal injury, particularly at a perianal site.

Continue nicorandil and treat with topical corticosteroids alone: Local anti-inflammatory therapy does not address the causal drug exposure; associated ulcers may persist until withdrawal.

Halve nicorandil and continue until the ulcer closes: Dose reduction alone is not the recommended response to recognized drug-related ulceration, which can progress to serious complications.

  • A — Continue nicorandil and add acid suppression: Acid suppression may treat acid-related upper GI disease but does not remove nicorandil-associated mucosal injury, particularly at a perianal site.
  • C — Continue nicorandil and treat with topical corticosteroids alone: Local anti-inflammatory therapy does not address the causal drug exposure; associated ulcers may persist until withdrawal.
  • D — Halve nicorandil and continue until the ulcer closes: Dose reduction alone is not the recommended response to recognized drug-related ulceration, which can progress to serious complications.

questions.question: Which comorbidity specifically argues against using trimetazidine as an add-on for chronic angina?
options: Parkinson disease with bradykinesia and rigidity
Sinus bradycardia without conduction disease
Low-normal blood pressure without hypoperfusion
Well-controlled diabetes without renal impairment
questions.explanation:
Trimetazidine and Movement Disorders

Correct answer: Parkinson disease with bradykinesia and rigidity

Neurological Restriction

**Trimetazidine can cause or worsen parkinsonian symptoms.**

Avoid in Parkinson disease, related movement disorders and severe renal impairment; withdraw if new motor symptoms emerge.

Clinical Role

**Use only as an add-on for stable angina where approved.**

It does not treat an acute attack or establish a reduction in MI or mortality.

**Reassess persistent neurological symptoms after withdrawal.**

A drug association does not exclude an independent neurological disorder requiring evaluation.

Sinus bradycardia without conduction disease: Trimetazidine has little direct heart-rate effect and may be considered when further slowing is undesirable, provided other contraindications are absent.

Low-normal blood pressure without hypoperfusion: Its limited hemodynamic effect can be useful when vasodilators are poorly tolerated; low-normal pressure is not the specific contraindication here.

Well-controlled diabetes without renal impairment: Diabetes alone is not the motor-disorder contraindication; treatment still requires an appropriate angina indication and clinical review.

questions.question: A stable patient with symptomatic HF and EF 30% takes enalapril. The clinician plans to replace it with sacubitril/valsartan. There is no history of angioedema. Which transition is required?
options: Stop enalapril and allow at least thirty-six hours before the first sacubitril/valsartan dose
Stop enalapril and begin sacubitril/valsartan twelve hours later
Stop enalapril and begin sacubitril/valsartan twenty-four hours later
Overlap reduced-dose enalapril with sacubitril/valsartan during initial titration
questions.explanation:
ACE Inhibitor Washout Before Sacubitril/Valsartan

Correct answer: Stop enalapril and allow at least thirty-six hours before the first sacubitril/valsartan dose

ACE Inhibitor–ARNI Transition

**Allow ≥36 hours after the last ACE inhibitor dose before ARNI.**

Overlapping neprilysin and ACE inhibition increases bradykinin-associated angioedema risk.

Prescribing Checks

**Do not overlap ARNI with an ACE inhibitor or additional ARB.**

Sacubitril/valsartan already contains an ARB.

**Check angioedema history, BP, potassium and renal function.**

The ACE washout is distinct from switching an ARB; titrate only as tolerated.

Stop enalapril and begin sacubitril/valsartan twelve hours later: A twelve-hour interval does not meet the required ACE inhibitor washout; concurrent effects on vasoactive peptide breakdown increase angioedema risk.

Stop enalapril and begin sacubitril/valsartan twenty-four hours later: A one-day interruption remains shorter than the specified thirty-six-hour minimum. The usual dosing interval of the ACE inhibitor does not define an adequate washout.

Overlap reduced-dose enalapril with sacubitril/valsartan during initial titration: Concomitant ACE inhibition and sacubitril/valsartan is contraindicated. Lowering either dose does not create a validated overlap strategy or remove the angioedema hazard.

questions.question: A stable, euvolemic patient with symptomatic HF and EF 30% has not previously taken an ACE inhibitor or ARB. BP is 116/72 mmHg, eGFR 48 mL/min/1.73 m² and potassium 4.4 mmol/L. Sacubitril/valsartan is selected. Which starting regimen matches the adult prescribing information?
options: Sacubitril/valsartan 49/51 mg twice daily
Sacubitril/valsartan 24/26 mg twice daily
Sacubitril/valsartan 97/103 mg twice daily
Sacubitril/valsartan 49/51 mg once daily
questions.explanation:
Select the Reduced ARNI Starting Dose for Minimal Prior RAS Exposure

Correct answer: Sacubitril/valsartan 24/26 mg twice daily

ARNI Starting Dose

**No or low prior ACE inhibitor/ARB exposure: start 24/26 mg twice daily.**

The reduced start reflects limited prior RAS blockade, not an automatic prohibition from moderate CKD.

Titration

**Increase every 2–4 weeks as tolerated toward 97/103 mg twice daily.**

Monitor hypotension, creatinine and potassium.

**Correct volume depletion and review interacting drugs.**

Do not omit an indicated ACE-inhibitor washout when one has actually been taken.

Sacubitril/valsartan 49/51 mg twice daily: This is the usual adult starting dose when no dose-reduction circumstance applies. Lack of prior ACE inhibitor or ARB exposure calls for half that usual starting dose.

Sacubitril/valsartan 97/103 mg twice daily: This is the target maintenance dose, not an appropriate initial regimen in a treatment-naive patient; initiation must account for hypotension and renal/potassium effects.

Sacubitril/valsartan 49/51 mg once daily: Reducing frequency is not the labeled adult low-start strategy. The lower-strength twice-daily regimen preserves the intended dosing schedule.

questions.question: A patient hospitalized with HF and EF 25% is now euvolemic and clinically stable, without inotropes, hypoperfusion, important bradycardia or AV block. There is no prior beta-blocker treatment. Which initial prescription uses an evidence-based agent, formulation and starting dose under AHA/ACC/HFSA 2022?
options: Bisoprolol 10 mg once daily
Metoprolol tartrate 12.5 mg twice daily
Metoprolol succinate extended release 12.5 mg once daily
Carvedilol 25 mg twice daily
questions.explanation:
Use an Evidence-Based Beta Blocker After Compensation

Correct answer: Metoprolol succinate extended release 12.5 mg once daily

Evidence-Based HFrEF Beta Blockers

**Metoprolol succinate ER, carvedilol and bisoprolol** have outcome evidence.

Metoprolol succinate 12.5 mg daily is an appropriate low start in this compensated patient.

Initiation and Monitoring

**Start after hemodynamic stabilization and titrate gradually.**

Check HR, BP, congestion and conduction; do not initiate during active hypoperfusion.

**Formulation matters.**

Metoprolol tartrate is not the trial-supported succinate extended-release regimen for HFrEF outcome treatment.

Bisoprolol 10 mg once daily: Bisoprolol is an evidence-based agent, but 10 mg daily is its target dose rather than the treatment-naive starting dose. Initiation generally uses 1.25 mg daily followed by tolerated titration.

Metoprolol tartrate 12.5 mg twice daily: Short-acting tartrate can be used for other clinical purposes, but is not interchangeable with the sustained-release succinate regimen carrying the specified HFrEF mortality evidence. A low dose does not remove the formulation distinction.

Carvedilol 25 mg twice daily: Carvedilol is an evidence-based agent, but 25 mg twice daily is a target-level regimen. A treatment-naive compensated patient generally starts at 3.125 mg twice daily and increases gradually with reassessment.

questions.question: A patient with NYHA II HF and EF 30% is receiving tolerated foundational treatment without an MRA. Repeat potassium is 5.2 mmol/L and eGFR is 42 mL/min/1.73 m². Under AHA/ACC/HFSA 2022 guidance, which plan is appropriate?
options: Start eplerenone 25 mg on alternate days with a potassium check in one week
Start spironolactone 12.5 mg daily with a potassium check in one week
Address reversible hyperkalemia and repeat laboratory assessment before starting an MRA
Replace the RAS inhibitor with an MRA after stopping the former
questions.explanation:
MRA Initiation Requires Both Renal and Potassium Eligibility

Correct answer: Address reversible hyperkalemia and repeat laboratory assessment before starting an MRA

MRA Eligibility

**Initiate when eGFR >30 mL/min/1.73 m² and potassium <5.0 mmol/L** under AHA/ACC/HFSA 2022.

Potassium 5.2 fails the entry threshold despite adequate eGFR.

Correct and Reassess

**Review supplements, salt substitutes, NSAIDs and renal changes.**

Repeat potassium after addressing reversible causes.

**Monitor closely after initiation or dose changes.**

If potassium cannot be maintained below 5.5 during treatment, discontinue the MRA to avoid life-threatening hyperkalemia.

Start eplerenone 25 mg on alternate days with a potassium check in one week: An alternate-day regimen can be appropriate with reduced renal function in an otherwise eligible patient. Eplerenone still raises potassium, so agent selection and a lower frequency do not remove the current initiation barrier.

Start spironolactone 12.5 mg daily with a potassium check in one week: Low-dose spironolactone with early surveillance can be appropriate after initiation criteria are met. Renal eligibility does not cancel the requirement for potassium below 5.0 mmol/L; monitoring cannot substitute for correcting the current elevation first.

Replace the RAS inhibitor with an MRA after stopping the former: Replacing one indicated class is not the default response to modest hyperkalemia. The current potassium level also constrains MRA initiation, so contributors and repeat values should be assessed before restructuring the complementary regimen.

questions.question: A stable patient with symptomatic HF and EF 32% has HbA1c 5.5%, eGFR 38 mL/min/1.73 m² and no volume depletion. Dapagliflozin is being considered for HF. Which plan is appropriate under its US prescribing information?
options: Start dapagliflozin 10 mg on alternate days
Start dapagliflozin 5 mg once daily
Start dapagliflozin 10 mg once daily
Defer initiation until eGFR is at least 45 mL/min/1.73 m²
questions.explanation:
SGLT2 Treatment for HF Does Not Require Diabetes

Correct answer: Start dapagliflozin 10 mg once daily

Dapagliflozin for HF

**Use 10 mg daily for the HF indication**, independent of diabetes.

The patient’s eGFR 38 permits initiation under the cited US label.

Safety

**Assess volume status, kidney function and ketoacidosis risk.**

Sick-day and perioperative interruption advice matters even without marked hyperglycemia.

**Glycemic efficacy and HF eligibility differ.**

A reduced glucose-lowering effect at lower eGFR does not remove established HF benefit; watch genital infection and dehydration.

Start dapagliflozin 10 mg on alternate days: Alternate-day dosing may appear a cautious response to CKD, but it is not the labeled HF regimen. At eGFR 38, use the indicated daily dose after assessing volume status and other safety considerations.

Start dapagliflozin 5 mg once daily: A 5-mg starting dose is used for glycemic control in eligible patients, but the adult HF regimen is 10 mg daily. Kidney function of 38 does not require a lower HF starting dose under the cited label.

Defer initiation until eGFR is at least 45 mL/min/1.73 m²: The eGFR 45 limitation concerns glycemic efficacy rather than the separate HF indication. The cited US label permits initiation for HF at this patient’s eGFR, with renal and volume monitoring.

questions.question: A patient with stable HFrEF and CKD starts an ACE inhibitor because ARNI is not feasible. Two weeks later, creatinine has risen from 1.5 to 1.8 mg/dL and is stable on repeat testing. Potassium is 4.6 mmol/L, BP 116/70 mmHg, and there is no hypovolemia or new illness. Which approach best fits KDIGO 2024 guidance?
options: Interrupt the ACE inhibitor and repeat renal testing after one week
Continue the ACE inhibitor with planned renal and potassium monitoring
Halve the ACE inhibitor dose and maintain the reduced dose
Replace the ACE inhibitor with an ARB to prevent the filtration change
questions.explanation:
A Modest Creatinine Rise After ACE Inhibition Requires Context

Correct answer: Continue the ACE inhibitor with planned renal and potassium monitoring

Creatinine After RAS Blockade

**Rise from 1.5 to 1.8 mg/dL = 20%.**

Stable BP, potassium and volume status support continuation with monitoring.

When to Investigate

**A rise >30% within four weeks warrants assessment** under KDIGO 2024.

Consider hypovolemia, NSAIDs, renal artery disease or intercurrent illness.

**Do not equate a small hemodynamic rise with progressive kidney injury.**

Reassess significant hypotension, hyperkalemia or continuing deterioration promptly.

Interrupt the ACE inhibitor and repeat renal testing after one week: Interruption can be necessary with progressive renal deterioration, significant hypotension or uncontrolled hyperkalemia. A stable 20% rise with acceptable pressure and potassium does not meet the cited creatinine trigger for routine interruption.

Halve the ACE inhibitor dose and maintain the reduced dose: Dose reduction may be appropriate when adverse effects persist after contributors are addressed. Here the change is within the cited acceptable early range, so automatic dose reduction sacrifices indicated treatment without a supplied intolerance.

Replace the ACE inhibitor with an ARB to prevent the filtration change: An ARB may substitute for ACE-inhibitor cough or other appropriate intolerance. Both reduce angiotensin-mediated efferent arteriolar tone, so changing classes does not inherently eliminate this hemodynamic filtration response.

questions.explanationHtml:
A Modest Creatinine Rise After ACE Inhibition Requires Context

Correct answer: Continue the ACE inhibitor with planned renal and potassium monitoring

Creatinine After RAS Blockade

  • Rise from 1.5 to 1.8 mg/dL = 20%.
    • Stable BP, potassium and volume status support continuation with monitoring.

When to Investigate

  • A rise >30% within four weeks warrants assessment under KDIGO 2024.
    • Consider hypovolemia, NSAIDs, renal artery disease or intercurrent illness.
  • Do not equate a small hemodynamic rise with progressive kidney injury.
    • Reassess significant hypotension, hyperkalemia or continuing deterioration promptly.

Other Options

  • Interrupt the ACE inhibitor and repeat renal testing after one week: Interruption can be necessary with progressive renal deterioration, significant hypotension or uncontrolled hyperkalemia. A stable 20% rise with acceptable pressure and potassium does not meet the cited creatinine trigger for routine interruption.
  • Halve the ACE inhibitor dose and maintain the reduced dose: Dose reduction may be appropriate when adverse effects persist after contributors are addressed. Here the change is within the cited acceptable early range, so automatic dose reduction sacrifices indicated treatment without a supplied intolerance.
  • Replace the ACE inhibitor with an ARB to prevent the filtration change: An ARB may substitute for ACE-inhibitor cough or other appropriate intolerance. Both reduce angiotensin-mediated efferent arteriolar tone, so changing classes does not inherently eliminate this hemodynamic filtration response.

References

  • KDIGO CKD guideline, 2024: RAS inhibitor monitoring
  • ACC HFrEF treatment consensus pathway, 2024

questions.question: A patient with HFrEF has recurrent treatment-limiting hyperkalemia despite correction of supplements and other reversible causes. The HF team considers patiromer to facilitate renin–angiotensin–aldosterone inhibitor treatment. Which interpretation of DIAMOND and AHA/ACC/HFSA 2022 guidance is most accurate?
options: DIAMOND randomized unselected patients before testing tolerance of RAAS inhibitor optimization
DIAMOND established reduced cardiovascular mortality as its definitive primary result
DIAMOND found potassium lowering but no improvement in maintaining MRA treatment
Patiromer can improve potassium control and treatment maintenance, but this does not establish an independent mortality benefit
questions.explanation:
Potassium Control and Proven HF Outcome Benefit Are Different Endpoints

Correct answer: Patiromer can improve potassium control and treatment maintenance, but this does not establish an independent mortality benefit

Potassium Binders in HFrEF

**Patiromer can reduce hyperkalemia and facilitate RAS-inhibitor/MRA use.**

DIAMOND primarily informs potassium control and treatment maintenance.

Evidence Boundary

**This does not establish an independent mortality benefit from the binder.**

Separate enabling disease-modifying treatment from directly proving improved clinical outcomes.

**Monitor potassium, magnesium and medication timing.**

Correct reversible causes and follow product-specific separation from other oral drugs.

DIAMOND randomized unselected patients before testing tolerance of RAAS inhibitor optimization: The study used a run-in incorporating patiromer and RAAS inhibitor optimization before randomized withdrawal. That selection affects generalizability to patients unable to complete optimization and differs from an unselected initiation trial.

DIAMOND established reduced cardiovascular mortality as its definitive primary result: The trial’s final primary endpoint was change in serum potassium, after alteration of the original outcome plan. Improved potassium-related results cannot be relabeled as a proven mortality reduction.

DIAMOND found potassium lowering but no improvement in maintaining MRA treatment: The trial assessed more than a laboratory difference: patiromer reduced MRA dose-reduction events as well as recurrent hyperkalemia. That treatment-maintenance finding should be preserved without inflating it into a mortality claim.

DIAMOND patiromer randomized trial, 2022 — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9622299/

AHA/ACC/HFSA heart failure guideline, 2022 — https://doi.org/10.1161/CIR.0000000000001063

KDIGO CKD guideline, 2024: RAS inhibitor monitoring — https://kdigo.org/wp-content/uploads/2024/03/KDIGO-2024-CKD-Guideline.pdf
